items.h: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) not seen practicing Thursday
items.s: Dontayvion Wicks was not seen at practice on Thursday. Wicks did not participate in Wednesday's walkthrough. He will need to be monitored in practice on Friday off a short week.

items.h: Absent for another practice
items.s: Wicks (ankle) isn't participating Thursday's practice, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports. Wicks hasn't practiced in any fashion since Week 6 while he continues to manage an ankle injury. Unless he's able to get back on the field in some capacity Friday, Wicks will likely be ruled out for a second straight game this Sunday at Washington.

items.h: Dontayvion Wicks' Ankle Keeps Eagles Receiver Picture Unsettled
items.s: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was not spotted warming up at Thursday's practice, according to Brooks Kubena of The Athletic, leaving his availability for Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Washington Commanders uncertain. He was listed as an estimated nonparticipant Wednesday after missing Monday night's loss to the Dallas Cowboys, and the veteran also missed all three practices before being ruled out against Dallas. If his continued absence from practice persists, Philadelphia would be relying on its remaining receiving options, including Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown, and Darius Cooper, with Brown drawing five targets against Dallas and Cooper three and both…

items.h: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) misses practice Wednesday
items.s: Dontayvion Wicks did not participate in Wednesday's walkthrough practice. Wicks was sidelined in Week 7 against the Cowboys. He'll need to be monitored in practice the rest of the week.

items.h: DNP on Wednesday
items.s: Wicks (ankle) didn't take part in Wednesday's walkthrough. Wicks thus has logged a DNP on four consecutive injury reports going back to last week as he deals with an ankle issue. He likely will need to practice in some capacity Thursday and/or Friday to have a chance to suit up Sunday at Washington.

items.h: Dontayvion Wicks is Absent from Wednesday's Walkthrough
items.s: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was a non-participant during Wednesday's walkthrough, according to Zach Berman. Wicks sat out the Week 7 loss to the Dallas Cowboys, and him being absent start of this week isn't a great start. The expectation is that he'll need to at least participate in a limited capacity to have a chance to play against the Washington Commanders in Week 8. The Eagles are banged up at wide receiver with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) absent during Wednesday's walkthrough as well. Makai Lemon could end up being the top wideout again. Fantasy managers will need to check back throughout the week for more updates on Wicks and Smith ahead of Sunday's game.

items.h: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) out for Week 7
items.s: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks was ruled out for Monday Night Football against Dallas due to an ankle injury. Wicks did not practice this week, so this does not come as a surprise. However, multiple important players will miss Week 7, including Wicks and wide receiver DeVonta Smith. Quarterback Tanner McKee will rely on a patchwork offense in a divisional matchup.

items.h: Ruled out for Monday's game
items.s: Wicks (ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's game versus the Cowboys. Wicks wasn't able to practice in any capacity during Week 7 prep due to an ankle injury and thus will miss his first contest of the campaign. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) also sidelined Monday, the Eaglges will rely on a receiving corps composed of Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore and Britain Covey, though TE Dallas Goedert (knee) may end being the favorite target of QB Tanner McKee.

items.h: Not spotted at Saturday's practice
items.s: Wicks (ankle) was not on the field for the start of Saturday's practice, Andrew DiCecco of Inside the Birds reports. It looks like both Wicks and DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will miss all three Week 7 practices, so the duo's chances of playing Monday against the Cowboys appears to be slim, but the Eagles will announce their injury designations following Saturday's session. Rookie Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper and tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) would all be involved more heavily in the offense if one or both of Wicks and Smith is sidelined.

items.h: Dontayvion Wicks Ruled Out for Week 7
items.s: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) has been ruled out for his team's Week 7 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday night. Wicks did not practice at all this week as he deals with an ankle injury. The 25-year-old has recorded 19 catches for 284 yards and a touchdown on 32 targets across six games this season and could have had a chance to be the Eagles' WR1 against Dallas. Instead, Philadelphia will be without both Wicks and star wideout DeVonta Smith (hamstring) on Monday night. The Eagles' injuries at wide receiver could open a path for rookie wideout Makai Lemon to assume a lead role in his team's passing game alongside tight end Dallas Goedert. Still, the…

items.h: Dontayvion Wicks Remains Sidelined With Ankle Injury
items.s: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) is difficult to trust in fantasy lineups for Monday night's matchup against the Dallas Cowboys after missing Saturday's practice, his third consecutive absence, according to Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer. He appeared positioned for more opportunities with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) also struggling to practice, but his own injury now threatens to keep him sidelined, and McLane previously indicated that Wicks was trending toward missing Monday's game. Wicks drew eight targets while Smith was absent in Week 5, catching five passes for 63 yards against the Jacksonville Jaguars. With Smith back and Tanner McKee starting in…

items.h: Wicks (ankle) didn't take part in Friday's practice.
items.s: With back-to-back DNPs to kick off Week 7 prep due to an ankle issue, Wicks has only one more opportunity to mix into drills Saturday before the Eagles potentially make a ruling on his status for Monday's contest against the Cowboys. Fellow WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) also hasn't practiced this week, leaving Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore and Britain Covey as the healthy options at the position on the active roster.

items.h: Wicks (ankle) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice.
items.s: Wicks made a very brief exit late in this past Sunday's loss to the Panthers but was able to return. With an ankle injury being cited as the reason for Thursday's absence, the nature of the injury has been revealed. Both Wicks and No. 1 WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) were DNPs to kick off Week 7 prep, so the situation bears watching to see if either of them will be able to play Monday against the Cowboys.

items.h: Wicks was not spotted during the portion of Thursday's practice open to the media, Jimmy Kempski of The Philly Voice reports.
items.s: The Eagles are holding a few key pass catchers out of practice Thursday, including Wicks, DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert. It could just be a rest day for those players, with clarification on any potential injuries to come on Thursday's injury report. If Wicks is dealing with an injury, he'll have an extra day to recover since the Eagles play Monday against Dallas.

items.h: Wicks caught two of four passes for 24 yards during the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
items.s: Wicks' 24 receiving yards were his second lowest of the season, but he still finished third among Eagles pass catchers in that category Sunday behind DeVonta Smith (75) and Dallas Goedert (61). Week 6 was the Eagles' first game with Tanner McKee under center, and with Jalen Hurts (calf) out for the rest of the season, the scoring floors of Wicks and the other Philadelphia pass catchers figure to be lower moving forward. That said, the Eagles have a juicy Week 7 matchup on Monday, Oct. 26 against the Cowboys, whose defense ranks in the bottom-10 in the league in fantasy points allowed per…

items.h: Wicks (undisclosed) returned to Sunday's contest versus the Panthers, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
items.s: Both Wicks and fellow WR Makai Lemon (undisclosed) visited the medial tent in the second half, but both of them were able to rejoin Week 6 action.

items.h: Wicks (undisclosed) went to the medical tent during Sunday's game versus the Panthers, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
items.s: Wicks was tripped up by a Panthers defender at the end of a catch and run in the fourth quarter, and he went down to the turf before going to the sideline. He had two catches (on four targets) for 24 yards before his departure.

items.h: Fantasy football Week 6 inactives: Jeremiyah Love, DJ Moore out
items.s: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.

items.h: Wicks (hamstring) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest versus the Panthers.
items.s: Wicks was limited Wednesday and didn't log any on-field work Thursday, but an uncapped session Friday has him in the clear for Week 6 action. He'll be welcoming back DeVonta Smith (hamstring) to the lineup, though, which may not allow Wicks to reach the 6.5 targets per game that he received during Smith's two-game absence.

items.h: Wicks (hamstring) is practicing Friday, Andrew DiCecco reports.
items.s: The extent of Wicks' participation is unclear, but it's at least a good sign relative to Thursday when he didn't practice at all. He was limited Wednesday, after playing through the injury in a Week 5 loss to Jacksonville. Fellow Eagle wideout DeVonta Smith (hamstring) also returned to practice Thursday, but it isn't clear if he has a real shot to play Sunday against the Panthers.

items.h: Wicks (hamstring) didn't practice Thursday, Zach Berman of The Athletic reports.
items.s: Wicks was limited on the final two Week 5 injury reports due to a hamstring issue, but he didn't carry a designation into the weekend and suited up for this past Sunday's loss to the Jaguars in London, earning an 84 percent snap share and hauling in five of eight targets for 63 yards. He opened this week as limited Wednesday, so his downgrade one day later may be cause for concern. Friday's practice report could unveil if Wicks is in danger of missing Sunday's contest against the Panthers.

items.h: Wicks (hamstring) practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday.
items.s: Wicks now has been listed as limited on three consecutive injury reports dating back to last week due to a hamstring issue, but he wasn't tagged with a designation for a Week 5 matchup with the Jaguars in London. He ended up earning an 84 percent snap share in that contest, which he parlayed into five catches (on eight targets) for 63 yards with top WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) out for a second game in a row. Wicks doesn't appear to be in danger of sitting out this Sunday versus the Panthers, but his status nonetheless will be monitored as the week goes on.

items.h: Wicks caught five of eight targets for 63 yards during Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.
items.s: Wicks led the team in targets, and he was able to match his season-high five catches in the defeat. The wide receiver also exceeded 60 receiving yards for the third time this season and first time since Week 2. Wicks has now caught 17 of 28 targets for 260 yards and a touchdown over his first five regular-season contests as a member of the Eagles.

items.h: Wicks (hamstring) doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London.
items.s: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) set to miss a second straight contest, Wicks, Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper should comprise Philly's three-wide sets against Jacksonville. Wicks paced the group in snaps and routes last Sunday against the Rams and saw five targets.

items.h: Head coach Nick Sirianni anticipates that Wicks (hamstring) "will be out there" at Friday's practice.
items.s: Sirianni confirmed that Wicks injured his hamstring during Thursday's session, and he wound up as a limited participant on the injury report. While it appears Wicks will get some work in Friday, his status for Week 5 will not be known until the Eagles release their final injury report of the week following Friday's practice.

items.h: Wicks was limited at Thursday's practice due to a hamstring injury, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
items.s: Wicks' addition to the injury report midweek indicates that he may have picked up the health concern at practice, but he joins DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Hollywood Brown (ankle) as banged-up players at the position. Currently, rookie first-rounder Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore and Britain Covey are the Eagles' healthy wide receivers.

items.h: Wicks caught three of five targets for 18 yards during Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams.
items.s: Wicks was slated to operate as the team's No. 1 wide receiver in Week 4 with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) sidelined. He finished third on the team in targets behind fellow wideouts Darius Cooper (7) and Makai Lemon (6), while his 18 receiving yards were a season low. Wicks will have an easier matchup in Week 5 against the Jaguars, regardless of whether Smith is available or not.

items.h: Wicks will operate as the top wide receiver against the Rams on Sunday due to the absence of DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Chris McPherson of the Eagles' official site reports.
items.s: Wicks has the second-most targets, catches and receiving yards on the Eagles behind Smith through the first three games of the regular season. Smith gutted through a hamstring injury against the Bears in Week 3, but the star wide receiver will observe Sunday's game from the sidelines, meaning Wicks, rookie first-rounder Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper are all in line for more offensive snaps and targets from Jalen Hurts.

items.h: Wicks recorded two receptions for 32 yards on five targets in Monday's 27-7 loss to the Bears.
items.s: Though he didn't find paydirt, Wicks played a critical role on the Eagles' lone scoring drive late in the second quarter, leading off the possession with a 13-yard catch and run. He was otherwise held in check while the game was still competitive, with his other reception coming in the fourth quarter when the Bears had built a 20-point lead. Through his first three games with Philadelphia, Wicks has produced a 9-179-1 receiving line on 15 targets.

items.h: Wicks caught five of six targets for 74 yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Titans.
items.s: While he wasn't able to get into the end zone, Wicks still had a strong showing as the Eagles' clear WR2 behind DeVonta Smith and ahead of rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon. The former Packer is looking good in his new offense, producing a 7-147-1 line on 10 targets through two contests, and Wicks will look to keep developing chemistry with Jalen Hurts in a Week 3 road trip to Chicago.

items.h: Wicks caught two of four targets for 73 yards and a touchdown Sunday in a 24-22 Week 1 victory against Washington.
items.s: Wicks didn't log a particularly high volume of targets, but he nonetheless put up a nice fantasy score thanks to a 64-yard connection with Jalen Hurts late in the first quarter and a nine-yard TD catch in the second. Hurts spread the ball around pretty evenly, hooking up with six different pass catchers, none of whom logged more than four receptions. It could play into Wicks' favor if the Eagles' new offense encourages Hurts to spread the ball around, though all of DeVonta Smith, Makai Lemon and tight end Dallas Goedert figure to need to be fed in addition to Wicks.

items.h: Wicks is listed as a starter on the Eagles' unofficial depth chart.
items.s: Philadelphia lists three starting wide receivers, with those spots going to Wicks, DeVonta Smith and rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon. Wicks had 581 receiving yards as a rookie with the Packers during the 2023 regular season and has failed to reach that mark since, posting only 415 receiving yards in the 2024 regular season and 332 yards in 2025. The 25-year-old wide receiver has an opportunity to play a larger role with his new team, which will kick off regular-season action Sunday against the Commanders.

items.h: Wicks stood out with his route running during the Eagles' joint practices with the Patriots last Wednesday and Thursday, Cayden Steele of NJ.com reports.
items.s: Though he was generally impressive in both practices, Wicks turned in one highlight-reel-worthy rep during Thursday's session, when he easily shook 1-on-1 coverage from New England cornerback Carlton Davis at the line of scrimmage for what would have been a big gain, per Henry McKenna of FoxSports.com. Acquired from the Packers in April and immediately signed to a one-year, $12.5 million extension, Wicks has been repping with the first-team offense for most of his first camp with the Eagles while No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith and rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon have been slowed by…

items.h: Wicks has impressed Jalen Hurts with his route-running ability and work ethic during training camp, Johnny McGonigal of NJ.com reports.
items.s: "He's got great work ethic. He's got great hunger," Hurts said Wednesday. "In the summertime, he was beating down the door, trying to spend that time and just work. He's twitchy. He can attack the ball. He runs great routes. It'll be exciting to see him work this season with the aggression that he has." Wicks has been working as the default WR1 in recent days, as DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon have both been sidelined by hamstring injuries, and Wicks has shown up big in contested-catch situations, using his long frame to win against defensive backs. He's expected to push first-round rookie…

items.h: Have skills, need opportunity: 10 fantasy football picks who just need a chance to shine
items.s: Matt Bowen and Tristan H. Cockcroft list players they are most excited about, if and when opportunity knocks.

items.h: Wicks will enter training camp competing for a key role in Philadelphia's receiving corps following the team's trade of A.J. Brown, Glenn Erby of USA Today reports.
items.s: Wicks was acquired by the Eagles via a trade with Green Bay before Brown's departure, and he signed a new one-year, $12.5 million contract upon arrival. With Brown gone, DeVonta Smith remains the clear No. 1 receiver, while rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon (hamstring) and tight end Dallas Goedert are strong candidates to absorb additional targets. Still, Wicks' versatility has drawn attention, with head coach Nick Sirianni comparing him to Keenan Allen during mandatory minicamp. The 25-year-old could emerge as the favorite for the No. 3 receiver role over Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore…

items.h: The Eagles agreed to terms Friday on a trade to acquire Wicks (concussion) from Green Bay in exchange for a 2026 fifth-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.s: Wicks will reportedly ink a new one-year, $12.5 million contract with Philadelphia, providing him a substantial pay raise. The soon-to-be 25-year-old wideout doesn't necessarily face an easier path to playing time with his new team, though that could change if rumors surrounding A.J. Brown as a potential trade candidate do ultimately materialize this offseason. Per the current state of the Eagles' roster, all of Brown, DeVonta Smith, Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore and TE Dallas Goedert represent target competition for Wicks, who tallied just a 30-332-2 line across 14 regular-season…

items.h: Wicks (concussion) finished the 2025 regular season with 30 catches for 332 yards and two touchdowns in 14 games.
items.s: A calf strain, an ankle sprain and a concussion did force Wicks to miss three contests and play fewer than 10 snaps in two others, but he was available for much of the year, and he still finished only third on the team with 46 targets during the regular season. Christian Watson saw more targets (55) than Wicks even though he sat for the first six games of the campaign. The 2023 fifth-round pick has yet to record 40 or more catches in a season across his three-year career.

items.h: Wicks (concussion) has been ruled out for Saturday's wild-card game at Chicago.
items.s: The Packer listed Wicks as questionable on their final injury report Thursday. They're now downgrading him to 'out', which could leave a few more snaps/routes for any combination of Christian Watson, Romeo Doubs, Jayden Reed and Matthew Golden.

items.h: The Packers list Wicks (concussion) as questionable for Saturday's wild-card game against the Bears, Wes Hodkiewicz of the team's official site reports.
items.s: Head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed prior to Thursday's practice that Wicks was still in concussion protocol, which was backed up by the wideout remaining a limited participant in the team's final practice of the week. Wicks still has a chance to play Saturday, but he'll need to be cleared for full contact in addition to gaining clearance from an independent neurologist before he's removed from the protocol. With Bo Melton (knee) and Savion Williams (foot) recently going on injured reserve and with Wicks potentially missing the postseason opener, the Packers could be left with Christian…

items.h: Wicks (concussion) was limited at Wednesday's practice.
items.s: After Wicks suffered a concussion Week 17 against the Ravens, he wasn't able to practice in any capacity before being inactive this past Sunday at Minnesota. He's now maintained his activity level from Tuesday's walkthrough to Wednesday, but he still has some hurdles to get past, including gaining clearance from an independent neurologist, in order to have a chance to play in Saturday's wild-card contest at Chicago.

items.h: Wicks (concussion) was estimated as a limited participant for Tuesday's walkthrough practice, Tom Silverstein of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reports.
items.s: Wicks suffered a concussion in the Packers' Week 17 loss to Baltimore and was inactive for Sunday's 16-3 loss to the Vikings in the regular-season finale. Prior to Tuesday's session, head coach Matt LaFleur told Ryan Wood of USA Today that Wicks remains in concussion protocol, but the wideout's ability to practice in some fashion represents progress. Wicks will have two more chances to upgrade to full activity as he aims to clear the five-step protocol ahead of Saturday's wild-card game against the Bears.

items.h: Wicks (concussion) is inactive for Sunday's game at Minnesota, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
items.s: Wicks didn't practice during Week 18 prep following the concussion that he suffered Saturday, Dec. 27 against the Ravens. With Wicks sidelined, Green Bay's available options at the position Sunday will be Christian Watson, Romeo Doubs, Jayden Reed, Matthew Golden, Bo Melton and Jakobie Keeney-James. Wicks' next chance for game action will take place in the wild-card round.

items.h: Wicks (concussion) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game at Minnesota, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
items.s: Wicks wasn't able to practice this week after he made an early exit from last Saturday's loss to the Ravens due to a concussion. With his third absence of the campaign imminent, he'll end his third regular season with a 30-332-2 line on 46 targets in 14 appearances. Wicks' next chance for game action is in the wild-card round on either Jan. 10 or 11.

items.h: Wicks (concussion) didn't practice Thursday.
items.s: Wicks thus hasn't practiced in any capacity since he suffered a concussion this past Saturday versus the Ravens. Considering he appears to have multiple hurdles to surpass in order to gain clearance from the protocol for head injuries, he may be in danger of missing his third game of the season Sunday at Minnesota.

items.h: Wicks (concussion) didn't participate in Wednesday's practice, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
items.s: Wicks was forced out of Saturday's loss to the Ravens in the second quarter and didn't return after undergoing a concussion evaluation. With no on-field work to speak of to kick off Week 18 prep, he appears to be on the outside looking in to suit up for Sunday's regular-season finale at Minnesota. Ultimately, the Packers may make a ruling on Wicks' availability by the time they post their final injury report of the week Friday.

items.h: Wicks (concussion) will not return to Saturday night's game against the Ravens.
items.s: Wicks exited the game just ahead of halftime after catching his lone target for seven yards. With Wicks done for the night, Matthew Golden and Bo Melton are next up for wideout snaps behind Romeo Doubs, Christian Watson and Jayden Reed.
